meta.name: Deadlock Mod Manager vs Grimoire
meta.title: Deadlock Mod Manager vs Grimoire: Which Deadlock Mod Manager?
meta.description: Deadlock Mod Manager and Grimoire cover the same features since V2, so the choice comes down to which interface you prefer. Try ours live and import your Grimoire setup in a minute.

better.question: Which is better, Deadlock Mod Manager or Grimoire?
better.answer: Since Deadlock Mod Manager V2, both apps cover the same ground: GameBanana installs, conflicts and load order, shareable profiles, hero skins with 3D previews, crosshairs, autoexec and match stats. Pick the interface you like using. You can try Deadlock Mod Manager's in the live preview on this page.

same.question: Is Grimoire the same as Deadlock Mod Manager?
same.answer: No, they are separate open-source projects, but they share roots. Deadlock Mod Manager started in December 2024 and Grimoire a year later. Grimoire took cues from Deadlock Mod Manager, and several Deadlock Mod Manager contributors have since helped build Grimoire too.

switch.question: Can I switch from Grimoire to Deadlock Mod Manager?
switch.answer: Yes, in about a minute. Open the Mods Library, choose Import from other mod managers and pick Grimoire. Deadlock Mod Manager finds your Grimoire library and brings over your mods with their enabled state and load order, your profiles and your crosshairs. Nothing in Grimoire is changed.

goBack.question: Can I go back to Grimoire, or use both?
goBack.answer: Yes. Both apps read and write the same mod-interchange format, so you can export from Deadlock Mod Manager and import into Grimoire, or move back and forth while you decide.

safe.question: Are both mod managers safe?
safe.answer: Both are open source, so anyone can read the code. Deadlock Mod Manager's Windows installer is code-signed through SignPath. Grimoire's README says its Windows installers are not code-signed yet and publishes SHA256 checksums instead.

hero.title: Deadlock Mod Manager vs Grimoire
hero.intro: Both apps do the job well, so pick the one you'd rather open before every match. You can try ours on this page and bring your Grimoire setup over in about a minute.

shared.title: Feature for feature, it’s (almost) a tie
shared.intro: Both apps cover what most players need. We think ours has a few extras and a bit more polish, but we're biased. If you're looking for a specific feature, it's probably on this list, and both apps have it.

features.gamebanana: Browse and install GameBanana mods in-app

roots.title: Why they feel so alike
roots.first: Deadlock Mod Manager came first. Starting in December 2024, it turned the community's manual modding know-how into one app: GameBanana installs, gameinfo.gi set up for you, and launching modded or vanilla. Over the next year it added Linux support, sound mods, shareable profiles and themes, and the community helped polish all of it.
roots.grimoire: Grimoire started in December 2025 and took plenty of cues from what worked in Deadlock Mod Manager. We took that as a compliment and pitched in. Core Deadlock Mod Manager contributors have helped build Grimoire too, which is part of why moving between the two apps is easy.

interface.title: So it comes down to the interface
interface.intro: Both apps are customizable, in different ways.

dmm.title: Deadlock Mod Manager: switch whole themes
dmm.body: Each theme is a complete look with its own colors, and most add their own artwork and sidebar logo, from the gold default to Bloodmoon's crimson. Switch with one click, or use the Background plugin to set your own image. The mod library is a dense list, which helps once you have a lot of mods.

grimoire.body: A dark interface with big image cards that you adjust piece by piece:

tryIt.intro: This is a working copy of the app. Install a mod, hit launch, or pick a theme under Settings → Themes.
tryIt.mobileNote: On a PC you can click through the live preview right here.

switch.title: Bring your Grimoire setup with you
switch.intro: Deadlock Mod Manager imports your Grimoire library directly, so you don't reinstall mods or rebuild profiles.

install.title: Install Deadlock Mod Manager
install.body: Get it from the <link>download page</link>. Keep Grimoire installed; nothing in it is changed.

import.title: Open the import
import.body: In the Mods Library, choose Import from other mod managers. Grimoire is detected automatically, or you can point to its data folder.

pick.title: Pick what comes over
pick.body: Mods keep their enabled state and load order. Profiles become DMM profiles with the same mods, and crosshairs land in your crosshair history.

play.title: Play
play.body: Mods the app can't match are imported as local mods; identify them to get updates, or leave them as they are. Then hit Launch modded.

lockIn.title: No lock-in, either way
lockIn.format: Deadlock Mod Manager and Grimoire both support the open mod-interchange format. Export your mods, profiles and crosshairs from one app and import them into the other.
lockIn.reimport: Changed something in Grimoire after importing? Run the import again: mods you already have are matched and updated in place, not duplicated.
lockIn.tryBoth: Try both and keep the one you like.

smallPrint.title: The small print

installer.title: Windows installer
installer.body: Ours is code-signed through SignPath. Grimoire's README says its installers aren't signed yet, so Windows shows an "Unknown publisher" warning.

linux.title: Linux packages
linux.body: We ship an apt repo, .deb, RPM, Flatpak, AUR, nixpkgs and Gentoo. Grimoire ships an AppImage, .deb, an apt repo, AUR and a Nix flake.

tech.title: Under the hood
tech.body: Deadlock Mod Manager is built on Tauri and uses your system's webview. Grimoire is an Electron app that bundles its own Chromium.
